newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

West Indian cricket manager Clive Lloyd says he is dissatisfied with the way Australian captain Mark Taylor handled alleged sledging by his team in the fifth test in Perth, and is considering lodging a complaint with the International Cricket Council overthe incident. Page 20.
The twelve Australian Rugby League loyal clubs pledged their support for the ARL yesterday, re-signing with the establishment until 1998. Page 20.

The French Davis Cup team had an urgent training session yesterday after it was revealed that Mark Woodforde would be joining Pat Rafter in the singles draw in today's Davis Cup tie. Woodforde, a left-hander, was a surprise choice to play both singles and doubles as many predicted his doubles team mate Todd Woodbridge would fill the role. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The new coach of the Australian hockey team Terry Walsh has vowed to improve on the team's recent performances by adopting the training methods of the national women's team. Walsh reaffirmed yesterday his goal is to guide the team to the gold medal in Sydney 2000. Page 43.
Discarded Test cricketer Ricky Ponting guided his Tasmania side to a 22-run win with 69 runs off 71 balls against the Canberra Comets in a one day match at Manuka oval yesterday. Page 43.

Hockeyroo player Alison Annan has been named the NSW Sports Federation athlete of the year after leading her team to the gold medal in Atlanta, where she scored eight goals to be the equal top scorer at the Olympics. Page 43.
THE AGE

VRC officials have informed popular trainer Lee Freedman that samples taken from his horse, Fashion Caf, tested positive to the stimulant, caffeine. Freedman says he has "considerable evidence" to present to the inquiry which has not been set yet. Page C8.

Australian Football team North Melbourne has expressed reservations over its planned move to Docklands stadium following calls from Carlton president John Elliott for Government financial assistance. The Victorian premier has ruled out any help, saying it s a matter for the private sector. Page C8.

Australian under-23 basketball team received good news in yesterday's draw after it managed to avoid meeting the US, Lithuania and Yugoslavia in the preliminary rounds at this year's championships in Melbourne. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN
World No.32, Todd Woodbridge, widely tipped to play the singles against France in the first-round tie starting at White City today, has pushed for the selection of his doubles partner Mark Woodforde.

A radical plan by Kevin Sheedy to hold an overseas AFL match for premiership points has gained the support of several clubs and the Seven Network. Seven's Melbourne head of sport Tim Worner yesterday said he could not foresee any problems in broadcasting the game to Australia, having already covered more than half a dozen overseas matches. Page 101.

Justin Madden, the AFL's oldest player at 35, has agreed in principle to signing a reduced one-year contract with Carlton for 1997. Another 13 matches will bring Madden's total to 300 senior appearances, enabling him to join the elite three-man-300-club with John Nicholls and Bruce Doull. Page 104
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian hockey player Alyson Annan was named NSW Athlete of the Year in Sydney yesterday, adding to the accolades she has already earnt since helping the national side win gold in the Atlanta Olympics. She has already been named Telstra Player of the year, NSW Sportswoman of the Year and Stix Player of the Series. Page 112.

The Australian Cricket Board has rescheduled the traditional Australia Day Test in Adelaide next year, sparking a huge outcry, after Sydney was announced as host of the New Year Test match for next season. Page 114.

After the annual City v Country match was abandoned, NSW Country Rugby Union president Chris Anderson cast around and has formed the Cockies in an effort to revive the NSW country competition. Ex-Wallaby Marty Roebuck has been recruited as coach with famed Test prop Jon While appointed as chairman of selectors and John Lambie and Stu Macdougall as directors. Page 114.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
